title: A split torus endomorphism is onto or has a nontrivial torus in its kernel
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. A maximal torus is a torus subgroup maximal under inclusion. Let $T$ be a torus and let $f:T\to T$ be a group-scheme homomorphism. Exactly one of the following holds: (i) $f$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented, meaning flat and surjective on spectra, locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]; (ii) the scheme-theoretic kernel $\ker f$, whose $A$-points are $\{t:f_A(t)=1\}$, contains a closed subtorus $S\simeq\mathbf G_m^s$ for some integer $s\geq1$. Case (i) includes inseparable isogenies in positive characteristic and the unique endomorphism of the trivial torus.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(b), printed pp.233--234, and Remark 12.5, printed p.232 (character groups and kernels); this is the torus-kernel alternative used in the proof of Theorem 17.48, printed p.367.

proof.text: Choose $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. The torus-matrix correspondence and character anti-equivalence identify $T=D_F(L)$, $L=\mathbf Z^r$, and $f=D_F(u)$ for $u=f^*:L\to L$; its coordinate pullback sends $e_m$ to $e_{u(m)}$ in $F[L]$. Apply the Smith-basis theorem over $\mathbf Z$ to $I=u(L)\subseteq L$ (take $N=I$, $O=L$). Obtain a basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $L$ and a basis $a_1b_1,\ldots,a_nb_n$ of $I$, with $0\le n\le r$ and all $a_i\ne0$ (a basis vector cannot be zero). Consequently the rational linear map $u_{\mathbf Q}:\mathbf Q^r\to\mathbf Q^r$ has image the span of $b_1,\ldots,b_n$: the displayed generators of $I$ are integer images, and every rational vector is an integer vector divided by a positive integer.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a), pp.233--234; the integer Smith-basis specialization is the cited Mathlib leaf, FreeModule/PID.lean:492.

proof.text: If $n=r$, $u_{\mathbf Q}$ is surjective, hence injective by the equal-finite-dimension linear-map theorem. Thus $u$ is injective, and $F[L]\to F[L]$, $e_m\mapsto e_{u(m)}$, is injective because distinct basis elements have distinct images. The structure morphism $T=\operatorname{Spec}F[L]\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ has affine source, so it is separated by the affine-source separatedness lemma; thus $T$ is a separated group scheme of finite type over $F$. Apply the group homomorphism factorization to $f=j\circ q$, with $q:T\to J$ faithfully flat and finitely presented and $j:J\hookrightarrow T$ closed. The scheme $J$ is affine by the affine description of a closed immersion. Its coordinate map $j^*:F[L]\to F[J]$ is surjective, and is injective because its composite with $q^*$ is the injective map $f^*$. It is therefore a ring isomorphism, whose inverse induces an inverse scheme morphism by affine spectrum functoriality. Hence $j$ is an isomorphism and $f=j\circ q$ has all the properties in (i).

source.place: Theorem 5.39 and Proposition 5.43(c) implies (a), pp.108--109; Theorem 12.9(a), pp.233--234, for the preceding coordinate identification.

proof.text: If $n<r$, put $s=r-n\ge1$ and let $p:L\twoheadrightarrow\mathbf Z^s$ send $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ to zero and the remaining basis vectors to the standard basis. Then $pu=0$ since $p$ annihilates the displayed generators of $I$. The character anti-equivalence turns the surjection $p$ into a closed immersion $D_F(p):D_F(\mathbf Z^s)\hookrightarrow D_F(L)=T$. Its source is $\mathbf G_m^s$ by the diagonalizable-group decomposition. Contravariant functoriality gives $f\circ D_F(p)=D_F(pu)$, the trivial homomorphism. This holds on every algebra's points, so the closed subtorus factors through the scheme-theoretic kernel, exactly (ii).

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a), pp.233--234; Remark 12.5, p.232, and the free-group case of the decomposition preceding it.

proof.text: For exclusivity, suppose (i). By the affine flatness criterion its coordinate map is flat; its spectrum is surjective by (i). The flat-surjective-spectrum criterion makes this ring map faithfully flat. Universal injectivity, applied to the ring as a module over itself, makes $f^*:F[L]\to F[L]$ injective. The basis formula forces $u$ injective. Clearing a common positive denominator of a rational kernel vector shows $u_{\mathbf Q}$ injective, hence surjective by the equal-dimension theorem. If a closed subtorus $S\simeq\mathbf G_m^s$, $s\ge1$, lay in $\ker f$, restriction of characters would be a surjection $v:L\twoheadrightarrow\mathbf Z^s$ by character anti-equivalence, with $vu=0$. For each $x\in L$, rational surjectivity gives $u(y)=d x$ for some $y\in L$, integer $d>0$. Hence $d v(x)=v(u(y))=0$, so $v(x)=0$ in the torsion-free group $\mathbf Z^s$, contradicting surjectivity. Thus (i) excludes (ii). When $r=0$ the first case applies with empty bases; in characteristic $p$, multiplication by $p$ has injective lattice map, so inseparable power maps are included without any smooth-kernel assertion.

source.place: Proposition 5.43, pp.108--109, and Theorem 12.9(a), pp.233--234; Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), algebra.tex Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings) and Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective).

lean.statement: theorem torusEndomorphism_kernel_dichotomy {F : Type u} [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (T : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) (hT : ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (T ≅ MultiplicativeType.splitTorus F r)) (f : T ⟶ T) : Xor (Flat f.hom.hom.left ∧ Surjective f.hom.hom.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f.hom.hom.left ∧ QuasiCompact f.hom.hom.left ∧ QuasiSeparated f.hom.hom.left) (∃ (s : ℕ) (i : (MultiplicativeType.splitTorus F s).X ⟶ GrpObj.ker f.hom.hom), 1 ≤ s ∧ IsClosedSubgroupScheme i)
lean.note: Uses the already landed splitTorus of def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type, added to stmt_deps. Xor expresses exactly one alternative; the second is an actual closed subgroup of GrpObj.ker f.hom.hom, with rank at least one. No new definitions or statement correction.
